paper_metadata.title: Shallow and Robust QAOA: Improving Feasibility and Hardware Performance via Linear-Chain and Ramp Schedules

experiments.description: Statevector simulation benchmark on a small VRP instance comparing standard QAOA, Two-Step QAOA, Grover-Mixer QAOA, Linear-Ramp Initialized QAOA, and Linear-Chain QAOA at depths p = 4, 6, and 8.

algorithm.variant: Standard QAOA / Two-Step QAOA / Grover-Mixer QAOA / Linear-Ramp Initialized QAOA / Linear-Chain QAOA
algorithm.ansatz: QAOAAnsatz; Grover-mixer uses Dicke-state preparation; LC filters nonadjacent ZZ terms
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not reported; optimized to low expectation value of the VRP cost Hamiltonian

hyperparameters.feasibility_metric: fraction of sampled bitstrings satisfying VRP constraints

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Standard QAOA initialized with gamma = pi, beta = pi/2; LRI-QAOA initialized with linear-ramp schedule; GM-QAOA initialized from Dicke state; Two-Step uses constraint-stage optimized parameters then frozen for cost stage

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary directed-edge variables x_ij indicate whether edge i -> j is selected; converted from DOcplex to QuadraticProgram to Ising Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x sum_{i,j} w_ij x_ij + lambda * sum_k (g_k(x))^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms for customer-visit, flow-conservation, depot-degree, and subtour constraints; Grover-Mixer and Two-Step additionally use feasible-subspace style constraint handling; LC removes nonadjacent ZZ interactions
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(z) = sum_i h_i z_i + sum_{i<j} J_ij z_i z_j + const

problem_instance.description: Small VRP with one depot, three customer nodes, and two vehicles; customer locations randomly placed on a 2D Euclidean plane; edge weights are squared Euclidean distances

dataset_specification.description: Random 2D Euclidean instance; solved classically with CPLEX to certify the optimum

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: DOcplex model converted to QuadraticProgram, then QUBO and Ising; coefficients normalized by dividing by the largest magnitude term
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Sampled 10,000 shots and ranked bitstrings by frequency; feasibility and rank of the known optimum reported

speedup_claims.conditions: Used only to certify the optimum for the small VRP instance
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime speedup comparison against CPLEX was made; CPLEX solve time was reported as only a few seconds.

experiments.description: Scalability experiment for LC-QAOA with linear-ramp initialization on a larger 5-node, 2-vehicle VRP, evaluated on IBM Rensselaer and IBM Fez for p = 17, 18, 19, and 20, with and without CVaR, using XpXm dynamical decoupling.

algorithm.variant: Linear-Chain QAOA with linear-ramp initialization and CVaR
algorithm.ansatz: Linear-chain QAOA ansatz with nearest-neighbor ZZ interactions only
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Linear-ramp initialization; CVaR used in some runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 30-qubit encoding with 20 decision variables and 10 slack variables
problem_formulation.objective_function: VRP cost with quadratic penalties; CVaR used as the optimization objective in some runs
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty-based QUBO; LC removes nonadjacent ZZ terms; XpXm dynamical decoupling applied; CVaR used to bias toward low-cost tail samples
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Ising Hamiltonian derived from the VRP QUBO

problem_instance.description: Larger VRP instance with 5 nodes and 2 vehicles

dataset_specification.description: Larger routing instance used to probe scaling; no further dataset details reported

noise_model.mitigation_details: CVaR compared against non-CVaR; XpXm applied for all runs
noise_model.noise_description: hardware noise; XpXm dynamical decoupling applied

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parameters transferred from simulation; CVaR used during optimization in some runs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Reported solution rank and feasibility percentage for each p and backend

speedup_claims.conditions: Used to certify the optimum only
speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime speedup comparison against CPLEX.
